title: Canonical symmetric-degree algebra on the affine basis
statement:
Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\mathcal E$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent]. Define the canonical affine-basis graded algebra $A_X(\mathcal E)$, in the graded algebra interface used for relative Proj [def-nagata-relative-proj], as follows. For every affine open $U$, set $R_U=\mathcal O_X(U)$, $M_U=\mathcal E(U)$ and $A(U)=\operatorname{Sym}_{R_U}(M_U)$. Its degree-$n$ submodule is $(\operatorname{im}\iota_{M_U})^n$, equivalently the image of the degree-$n$ tensor component [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Its structural $R_U$-algebra map is the canonical symmetric-algebra unit. For $U\subseteq V$, its restriction is the unique ring homomorphism sending scalars by $R_V\to R_U$ and $\iota_{M_V}(m)$ to $\iota_{M_U}(m|_U)$. These rings identify canonically with the affine sections of the symmetric algebra sheaf [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-symmetric-algebra].

The named well-definedness properties of this construction are that restriction preserves each degree and, since $\mathcal E$ is quasi-coherent, each restriction is coefficientwise base change: $R_U\otimes_{R_V} A(V)_n\to A(U)_n$, $r\otimes a\mapsto r\,a|_U$, is an isomorphism for every $n$. Restriction identities and composition are inherited from the symmetric-algebra presheaf. The homogeneous decomposition is the unique inverse of the summation map of the internal direct sum, and the rings, grades and restriction homomorphisms are the specified formulas, not data chosen from an existence assertion.

proof.text: Use the internal symmetric-degree decomposition of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-graded]. Rewriting the images of tensor grades as powers of the range of the symmetric inclusion gives sectionGradedAlgebra.

The scalar and degree-one equations for the canonical restriction of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction] prove degree preservation by Submodule.pow_induction_on_left': scalars have degree zero, addition preserves the asserted degree, and multiplying a degree-i element by an inclusion generator gives degree i+1. This constructs gradedRestriction.

Use the existing exists_sectionTensorEquiv of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-affine-section-comparison], now public in its original module. It identifies O(U) tensor Sym(E(V)) with Sym(E(U)), sending r tensor a to r times restriction(a). This reuses its affine-section and symmetric-algebra base-change proof rather than repeating it.

Bundle restriction as a graded algebra homomorphism and apply Mathlib GradedAlgHom.liftEquiv. The resulting graded homomorphism from the tensor-product graded algebra is the bijection of the previous step, by tensor induction. A bijective graded ring homomorphism is bijective on every homogeneous component: injectivity follows from the underlying injection, and for a homogeneous target choose a preimage and take its component of the same degree, using DirectSum.decompose_map. Compose this component equivalence with DirectSum.toBaseChange_bijective to identify O(U) tensor A(V)_n with A(U)_n. The pure tensor equation at 1 gives IsBaseChange.of_equiv, hence IsGradedBaseChangeAlong. No flatness or finite-generation hypothesis is required.

Assemble the fixed section rings, grades and restrictions into GradedAlgebraData of [def-nagata-relative-proj]. Identity and composition are those of the presheaf of [lem-weil-pbc-symmetric-algebra-sheaf-construction], and the preceding degreewise base-change theorem supplies the last field.
